info.name: Microservices – Lab 7
info.description:
Lab 7 – API Gateway, Service Discovery & Cloud Deployment

All requests go through the API Gateway at {{gatewayBaseUrl}}.
Do NOT call user-service, product-service, or order-service directly.

Set the 'gatewayBaseUrl' variable:
  Local Docker:  http://localhost:4000
  Cloud:         <your public gateway URL>

variable.description: Base URL of the API Gateway. Change to cloud URL for cloud testing.

item.name: 1. Gateway Health
item.description: Verify the API Gateway itself is running and reports its service registry.

request.description:
Handled locally by the gateway — NOT proxied to any upstream service.
Expected: 200 { status: 'UP', service: 'api-gateway' }

item.name: 2. Gateway → User
item.description: All user operations proxied through the gateway to user-service:3001 (internal).

request.description:
Gateway → user-service POST /users
Expected: 201 { user: { id, name, email } }

Gateway → user-service GET /users/1
Expected: 200 { user: { id: 1, name, email } }

Gateway → user-service PUT /users/1
Expected: 200 { user: { id: 1, name: 'Alice Johnson', email } }

Gateway → user-service DELETE /users/1
Expected: 200 { message: 'User deleted successfully', id: 1 }

item.name: 3. Gateway → Product
item.description: All product operations proxied through the gateway to product-service:3002 (internal).

request.description:
Gateway → product-service POST /products
Expected: 201 { product: { id, name, price, description } }

Gateway → product-service GET /products/101
Expected: 200 { product: { id: 101, ... } }

Gateway → product-service PUT /products/101
Expected: 200 { product: { id: 101, price: 34.99, ... } }

Gateway → product-service DELETE /products/101
Expected: 200 { message: 'Product deleted successfully', id: 101 }

item.name: 4. Gateway → Order
item.description:
All order operations proxied through the gateway to order-service:3003 (internal).
Order Service still performs inter-service REST validation (User + Product) using Docker DNS — this is unchanged from Lab 6.

request.description:
Gateway → order-service GET /orders/1001
Expected: 200 { order: { id: 1001, ... } }

item.name: 5. Error Handling
item.description: Tests for error scenarios: invalid references and gateway 502 when upstream is unreachable.

request.description:
Gateway → user-service GET /users/99999
Expected: 404 { error: 'User not found' }

MANUAL SETUP REQUIRED:
  docker compose stop user-service

Then send this request.
Expected: 502 { error: 'Service unavailable', service: 'user-service' }

The gateway returns a clean JSON 502 instead of a connection error.

Restore with:
  docker compose start user-service

Gateway catch-all 404 for routes not registered in the gateway.
Expected: 404 { error: 'Not found', availableRoutes: [...] }

item.name: 6. Service Discovery / Configuration
item.description:
Documents the configuration-based service discovery pattern.
Changing USER_SERVICE_URL / PRODUCT_SERVICE_URL / ORDER_SERVICE_URL env vars
reroutes the gateway without touching server.js.

item.name: GET /health — Verify Service Registry in Response

request.description:
The /health response includes 'upstreamServices' showing the current service registry values.
This is how you can verify that gateway is pointing at the correct service locations.

Configuration Change Demonstration:
1. Stop the stack: docker compose down
2. Edit compose.yaml USER_SERVICE_URL to point at a different valid host
3. Rebuild: docker compose up -d
4. Call GET /health — upstreamServices.user-service will reflect the new URL
5. Call GET /users — still works (or returns 502 if the new target doesn't exist)
No changes to api-gateway/server.js were required.
